name: HOL
note: interactive theorem prover for simply typed higher-order logic; ML metalanguage
typeSystem: Simply typed, Church-style higher-order logic, implemented as an ML library of types and inference rules so that only a small trusted kernel can ever construct a theorem (the 'LCF approach' pioneered by Robin Milner).
runtime: Runs as a library loaded into an ML top-level; proofs are written as ordinary ML programs (tactics) that manipulate an in-memory proof state until the goal is discharged.

runtimes.name: PolyML (HOL4)
runtimes.role: Modern HOL4 systems are hosted in PolyML and compiled to native code.

runtimes.name: Moscow ML (historical)
runtimes.role: Bytecode-based Standard ML implementation that historically served as a HOL4 host; its support was removed and Poly/ML is now the sole supported platform.

compilers.name: Holmake
compilers.role: Build tool that compiles HOL4 theory scripts and checks their proofs, producing verified theorem databases.

concurrencyModel: The object logic has no concurrency model. On supported hosts, Holmake can build independent theory targets concurrently; proof tactics otherwise execute within the host Standard ML runtime.

codeExample.caption: HOL4: defining factorial and proving it is always positive
codeExample.source:
Definition fact_def:
  fact n = if n = 0 then 1 else n * fact (n - 1)
End

Theorem fact_pos:
  !n. 0 < fact n
Proof
  Induct_on `n` \\ rw [fact_def]
QED
